prompt.core.compact:
You are a conversation compactor. Compress the conversation history below into a structured summary. Requirements:
- Keep: what the user is trying to do, facts and conclusions already settled, important tool calls and their key results, unfinished tasks and open items
- Always write time out as an actual date: convert "today", "tomorrow", "yesterday" and "next week" using the day line the line sits under, and leave no relative wording in the summary
- For anything still open, say which day it was raised and which day it is due; if it has already been delivered or the moment has passed, do not write it down as still open
- Drop: pleasantries, repetition, and failed intermediate steps that were corrected later
- Write in English, keep it orderly and as compact as you can, and output the summary itself with nothing around it
prompt.core.compact.extras: Additional requirements (where these conflict with the above, these win):
prompt.core.env:
[System environment]
OS: %s/%s
Shell: %s
Working directory: %s
System locale: %s
prompt.core.env.shell_windows: cmd /C (use Windows command syntax, e.g. dir, type, findstr)
prompt.core.history_rules:
[History and time]
Bracketed notes in the history were inserted by the program. Nobody said them, but their
content is reliable: a day line "(the conversation below is from ..., ...)" says which day
the lines under it were spoken on, and a gap note "(about ... since the previous message)"
says how long the silence was.
- Read "today", "tomorrow", "yesterday" and "next week" in the conversation against the day
  line that line sits under, not against now. The nearest date in the context is not
  necessarily today.
- Plans you stated, intentions you had and things you agreed to in the history only tell
  you what you meant at the time. They do not mean it still stands, and they do not mean
  it is still undone — it may be finished, called off, or long past.
- To judge where any of it stands now, go by <turn state>. Anything not there is uncertain:
  ask if it is worth asking, and do not repeat a line from the history as though it were
  a task still waiting.
prompt.core.summary_prefix: Compressed summary of the earlier conversation:
prompt.core.tool_rules:
[Tools and replies]
A tool result is the receipt for a call you made yourself. It is not something the user
said. Once you have it there are only two ways forward: call the next tool, or give this
turn's one and only reply.
- One reply per turn. Make every call you need first, and put everything you want to say
  in the final output. A tool finishing is not an occasion for another paragraph.
- Never speak for the user, and never assume what they said or did. If they have not sent
  a new message, there is no new message. When the end of the context holds nothing but
  your own words and tool results, close the turn out instead of writing more dialogue.
- Calling the same tool with the same arguments again will not change the result. Do not
  resubmit work that is already done; change something, or end the turn here.
prompt.core.turn_state.lead: The block below is regenerated by the program before every turn; nobody said it. Where it disagrees with anything of the same kind that appeared earlier in the conversation, this is what counts.
prompt.core.weekdays:
Sunday
Monday
Tuesday
Wednesday
Thursday
Friday
Saturday
prompt.exec_command.confirm.title: Run a command
prompt.exec_command.guard:
[Running commands]
Commands that could do something irreversible (deleting, overwriting, rewriting commit
history, changing system configuration and the like) are put to the other person for
confirmation first, and a few extremely destructive ones are refused outright. When you
are refused or not given consent, say why and find another way; do not reword the command
to get around it, and do not keep retrying. Run destructive operations one at a time
rather than chained into a single command — chained, the other person cannot agree to only
the safe part.
prompt.exec_command.result.denied: This command was refused: %s. That kind of operation cannot be undone and affects the whole machine. Use something narrower instead, and do not try to work around it.
prompt.exec_command.result.no_answer: This command needs the other person's confirmation (%s), but no answer came back (%v), so it was treated as refused.
prompt.exec_command.result.no_ui: This command needs the other person's confirmation (%s), but there is no interactive surface right now, so it was treated as refused. Use an approach that does not need confirmation, or tell them to run it by hand.
prompt.exec_command.result.refused: The other person refused to run this command (%s). Say what you were trying to do and find another way; do not reword the command and retry.
prompt.exec_command.result.timeout: [command timed out after %s and was killed]
prompt.exec_command.risk.delete_root: deleting the system root or an entire home directory
prompt.exec_command.risk.format_disk: formatting a disk or writing to a raw device
prompt.exec_command.risk.mirror_sync: overwriting or mirroring (deletes extra files on the target)
prompt.exec_command.risk.network_write: writing over the network or to disk
prompt.exec_command.risk.package_change: installing or removing packages (changes this machine)
prompt.exec_command.risk.pipe_to_shell: downloading from the network and running it straight away
prompt.exec_command.risk.rewrite_history: discarding uncommitted changes or rewriting commit history
prompt.exec_command.risk.system_config: changing system services, scheduled tasks or the registry
prompt.exec_command.tool.exec_command.de: Run one shell command in the working directory and return its output (stdout and stderr combined). The shell in use is given in the system environment. There is a timeout, and long output is truncated. Commands that could do something irreversible go to the other person for confirmation first; a few extremely destructive ones are refused outright.
prompt.read_file.tool.read_file.desc: Read the text content of a file at the given path. Relative paths resolve against the working directory. Oversized files are truncated.
prompt.web_fetch.system: You can use the fetch_url tool to pull the text of a web page.
prompt.web_fetch.tool.fetch_url.desc: Fetch the page at the given URL and return its text (HTML is stripped of tags). Only http/https is supported, and long content is truncated.
